title: 20X Anatomic and Layer Identification for Biocytin Filled Cells
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bey9jfz6
materials: Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework (mouse only)

steps.title: Draw soma, pia, and WM borders
steps.instruction: On the brightfield image, circle the soma with a pink polygon and draw the Layer 6/white‑matter (WM) border as a blue line below the cell; then, using the DAPI image, draw an orange line at the pia above the soma that matches the approximate width of the WM line. These annotations will later be used for an upright transformation aligning the reconstructed neuron to the pia.

substeps.instruction: Circle the soma with a pink polygon on the brightfield image.
Draw the Layer 6/white‑matter border as a blue line below the cell.
Reference the DAPI image and draw an orange line at the pia above the soma, matching the width of the WM line.

steps.title: Delineate cortical layers
steps.instruction: Using the DAPI image, first draw Layer 4 and Layer 5; then, on the brightfield image, draw the remaining cortical layers as blue polygons, each with the same width as the pia and WM drawings and wide enough to fully contain the cell of interest. These polygons are later used to calculate the cell’s layer‑distribution pattern.

substeps.instruction: Reference the DAPI image and draw Layer 4 and Layer 5.
Switch to the brightfield image and draw the remaining layers as blue polygons.
Ensure all layer polygons have the same width as the pia and WM lines and fully encompass the cell.

steps.title: Place cells in Allen CCF
steps.instruction: For mouse tissue only, match the experimental slice (using the 20X image) to a virtual slice in the Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework by aligning anatomical landmarks and adjusting slice angle, pitch, and yaw; once the virtual slice aligns, assign the appropriate cortical layer and brain region to the biocytin‑filled cell.

substeps.instruction: Using anatomical landmarks, align the 20X experimental slice to a virtual slice in the Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework, adjusting slice angle, pitch, and yaw as needed.
After the virtual slice matches the experimental slice, assign the cell’s layer and brain region.
